source.title: Array .chunk() expression should reject fractional and infinite sizes

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Phenomenon

The `chunk()` array expression extension validates its size argument with
`typeof chunkSize !== 'number' || Number.isNaN(chunkSize) || chunkSize <= 0`.
This lets fractional values (for example `2.5`) and non-finite values (for
example `Infinity`) through. Instead of being rejected, those values are used
directly as the loop step in `for (let i = 0; i < value.length; i += chunkSize)`
and as the bound in `value.slice(i, i + chunkSize)`. `Array.prototype.slice`
truncates fractional indices, so the returned groups are uneven and do not match
the requested size, and the call completes silently with no error.

### Minimal reproduction

In any expression that has an array in scope:

```
{{ [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].chunk(2.5) }}
```

Actual result: `[[1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]` — groups of two and three, with no error.

```
{{ [1, 2, 3].chunk(1/0) }}
```

Actual result: `[[1, 2, 3]]` — a single group, with no error.

Fractional sizes are easy to reach when the size comes from upstream data, such
as a computed batch size or a number read from a JSON field. Note that `chunk(0)`,
`chunk(-1)`, `chunk(NaN)` and `chunk("5")` are already rejected today.

### Expected behavior

`chunk()` should reject any size that is not a positive integer with a clear
`ExpressionExtensionError`, consistent with the existing rejection of `0`,
negative numbers, `NaN` and non-numeric values. The error message should refer
to a "positive integer" rather than a "positive numeric" argument.

### Impact

Workflows that split items into batches with `chunk()` receive silently
malformed groups: some batches are larger or smaller than requested, and with
`Infinity` the entire array is placed into one group. Because no error is raised,
the problem is hard to notice and downstream nodes operate on the wrong batch
boundaries, producing uneven API payloads or skipped/duplicated items. Both the
`n8n-workflow` copy of the extension and the `@n8n/expression-runtime` mirror
are affected, so the behaviour is the same regardless of the expression engine.

comments.author: grinem
comments.text: Spot on analysis. Swapping the guard to `!Number.isInteger(chunkSize) || chunkSize <= 0` cleanly handles floats, `Infinity`, `NaN`, and non-numbers in a single check without needing multiple conditions.
